transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, I'm only here because the campus health center made me come. I just feel like if I don’t keep really tight control over what I eat, I’ll gain weight and everything I’ve worked so hard for will fall apart.
Do you find yourself eating large amounts of food in a short period of time and feeling like you cannot stop, or is your main focus on strictly limiting the amount and types of food you consume?

No, I never lose control or eat large amounts of food like that; my focus is entirely on strictly limiting what I eat. Most days I just have black coffee, half a granola bar between classes if I feel faint, and a tiny salad at night. I even keep a spreadsheet on my laptop to make sure I stay under a very strict calorie limit.
How do you feel about your current body weight and shape, and do you feel that these factors have an undue influence on how you judge your self-worth?

Even though everyone says I'm too thin and my clothes are hanging off me, when I look in the mirror I still see soft areas and feel like I need to lose a little more. My self-worth is completely tied to the scale—if my weight is down, I feel worthy of my honors program and my future career, but if it goes up even half a pound, I feel disgusting and undeserving of being on campus.
